identity: The Nantun Wenchang temple at100WenchangStreet nearWanheTemple; NOT Beitun/Sizhangli WenchangTemple.

officialPages.evidence: Official exact Nantun identity and present raised, gallery-style building; original shrine history does not imply current facade is Qing-era.

officialPhotos.visualInspection: Direct official oblique facade photo inspected. Low ochre tile roof, cream/gray round columns, dark carved door panels, red lanterns and a black/gold文昌公廟plaque.

Direct official full-front photo inspected. Raised terrace, broad central access steps, white/gray stone balustrades and low carved relief panels. A rainbow fabric canopy and event banner obscure the center; treat those as temporary, not architecture.

distinguishingMotifs: Low, broad ochre/orange tiled roof with restrained upturned corners; less exuberant than Wanhe roof ornament.
A raised terrace with prominent pale stone railings and steps at the front.
Gray/cream columns frame several dark wooden door bays with carved panels.
A horizontal black-and-gold文昌公廟plaque and red round lanterns sit under the eave.
Lower facade/terrace wall includes pale relief panels and a solid reddish stone base.
